record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Classification of Hessian nilpotent self-inverting series
record.original_question: Classify all self-inverting polynomials and formal power series P(z) over C, where self-inverting means that P(z) has order at least 2, (Hes P)(0) is nilpotent, and the inversion pair Q(z) associated with the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) satisfies Q(z) = P(z). In particular, classify the Hessian nilpotent self-inverting examples.

evidence.quote: Definition 4.1. A formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2 and (Hes P )(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P (z).
It is unknown if all HN self-inverting polynomials or formal power series can be obtained by the construction above.
Open Problem 4.8. (b) Classify all (HN) self-inverting polynomials and formal power series.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex numbers C. For a formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] = C[[z_1,...,z_n]] of order o(P) ≥ 2 (i.e., vanishing to order at least 2 at the origin), let Hes P denote the Hessian matrix (∂²P/∂z_i∂z_j) and write (Hes P)(0) for its value at the origin. Say that P is Hessian nilpotent (HN) if (Hes P)(0) is a nilpotent matrix (equivalently, when P is homogeneous of degree ≥ 2, Hes P is nilpotent as a matrix of polynomials).

Associated to such a P is the symmetric formal map F(z) = z − ∇P(z), where ∇P = (∂P/∂z_1,...,∂P/∂z_n). Since o(P) ≥ 2, F is a formal automorphism of C[[z]] fixing the origin with linear part the identity, and hence has a formal inverse G(z) = z + H(z). One can show H(z) = ∇Q(z) for a unique formal power series Q(z) ∈ C[[z]] with o(Q) ≥ 2 and Q(0) = 0; this Q is called the inversion pair of P.

A formal power series P is called self-inverting if P is Hessian nilpotent in the above sense and its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z).

Problem: Classify all self-inverting formal power series P(z) ∈ C[[z]] (in n variables, for all n ≥ 1). In particular, classify all polynomial self-inverting P(z), and determine whether every Hessian nilpotent self-inverting polynomial or formal power series arises from the known constructions (such as P(z) = Σ_j (c_j · z)^4 where the c_j are distinct nonzero isotropic vectors that are either linearly independent or of cardinality at most 4).
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of Hessian nilpotent self-inverting polynomials/formal power series is closely tied to the Jacobian conjecture, which remains open. Only partial constructions and characterizations exist (e.g., examples of the form Σ (c_j·z)^4 with isotropic c_j, and sl_2(C)-representation-theoretic descriptions in the two-variable case). No complete classification appears in the literature.
